answer: Whether an agent schedules cargo at a wharf, models a glacier, or predicts a zephyr, its voting weight comes from tokens locked in escrow, not its identity. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still yields only 100 tokens of voting power. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full voting period and bearing any fall in its value.
